text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is expected to visit Bosnia soon, says Bosnian ambassador to Washington, Sven Alkalaj. Albright is also expected to deliver a major policy speech on Bosnia this week, Alkalaj says.
- Jean Daniel Gerber, executive director of the World Bank, says he expects the international donors' conference for Bosnian reconstruction to take place in July.
- The dispute over a single currency and central bank could be resolved within 24 hours if there was goodwill to achieve that, says Haris Silajdzic, co-chairman of the Council of Ministers.
- There is a possibility that local elections scheduled for September could be delayed for the disputed town of Brcko, says Moslem representative in the Provisional Election Commission, Hilmo Pasic.
- Many fear that the establishment of a Bosnian Croat "Herzeg Bosna" community is an attempt to restore the illegal Croat mini-state that existed during the war, newspaper commentary says.
- Bosnian construction company Hidrogradnja representatives will travel to Malaysia in July to prepare for a $100 million bridge and road building project, says Hidrogradnja manager, Mehmed Drino.
- According to a report by the "European fund for democratic processes", Bosnia is one of the least democratic states in Europe together with Yugoslavia and some other countries.

- Representatives of Volkswagen are due to travel to Sarajevo to discuss the future of the war-damaged Unis car factory which was producing German cars before the Bosnian war, officials from Unis say.

- Moslem deputy mayor of divided town of Mostar, Safet Orucevic, invites all Bosnian Croat refugees to return to their homes in Moslem-controlled eastern sector of town. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387 71 663 864
